conviction_note: Fiscal Q4 (Sept qtr) is near-determined by an Aug guide of $375M +/- $20M that KLIC has met at the top end before, and its OSAT customer ASE grew strongly in October. The stock turns on the first December-quarter guide and FY27 framing from a CEO in the job since Sept 1, inside a packaging-equipment de-rating (stock -50% from high, Besi roughly halved since June) and a put skew of 24 vol points. The evidence points both ways, so p_up is 51 and abs_move is 10.5, a little above the 10.1 implied because this name's own prints have reached 19%. The findings sum (+0.3) and the scaled number (+0.2) agree in sign and size because neither has an edge.
bar: FQ4 FY26 (Sept qtr): revenue $375M and non-GAAP EPS $1.44 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421185/kulicke-and-soffas-whisper-tops-guidance-as-battered-stock-tests-the-fy27-upturn-story). Benzinga lists $376.4M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KLIC/earnings-forecasts). Company guide 2026-08-05: $375M +/- $20M, non-GAAP EPS about $1.42, range $1.28-1.56 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/kulicke-and-soffa-industries-nasdaqklic-releases-q4-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-05/). The whisper is $1.61, above the top of the guide. There is NO sourced consensus for the December-quarter guide (FQ1 FY27), which is the line the stock trades on, so the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 4.2% of free float with 3.7 days to cover and a 0.49% borrow fee (ORTEX, 2026-10-22, https://app.ortex.com/s/Nasdaq/KLIC). shortsqueeze.com gives 2.17M shares short and 2.6 days to cover (2026-10-16, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=KLIC). Not crowded, so a squeeze is a small factor. Baseline: 25d skew +23.9 vol points (downside bid), put/call OI 0.25 (calls dominate a thin 1,192 OI), event-implied move 10.11% (ATM spread 57% of mid, indicative only), run-up -9.6% over 5d and -18.8% over 20d, -50.6% from the 52-week high. Sentiment is depressed and the skew says downside is paid for.

findings.finding: On the Aug 5 call management said purchase orders extend into fiscal Q2 2027 (the March 2027 quarter) and that above-average demand should last through at least the first half of FY27. That argues for a December-quarter guide near or above the $375M September guide, while the market price (-50% from the high) implies scepticism that the upturn lasts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 5 print raised the guide from $290-330M to $375M and the stock fell 3.39%. Earlier raises bought +4.66% (May 2026) and +19.27% (Feb 2026). Recent raises have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This is public since August, so it is partly priced. The 50% drawdown and +24 put skew say the market doubts it will hold. If the market believed it, the stock would sit near its post-August range ($81-103) rather than $66.
findings.independence: ASE's October revenue (separate finding, separate document) points the same way, https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/ase-technology-october-2026-revenue-rises-47-1-percent-to-88-6-billion

findings.finding: ASE, the largest OSAT and a KLIC customer segment, reported October 2026 revenue of NT$88.6B, +47.1% y/y and +0.6% m/m, with ATM (assembly/test) +7.9% m/m and +57.7% y/y (released Nov 10). This is the first look at customer activity in KLIC's December quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No KLIC-specific history on OSAT monthly data. It is a utilisation proxy for wire-bonder demand.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out after KLIC last spoke, but it is a widely published monthly series. The stock fell about 10% in the 5 days after it, so the market is not treating OSAT strength as KLIC strength. If it were priced as a read-through, the stock would not have kept falling.
findings.independence: Proxy: OSAT revenue, not KLIC tool orders. ASMPT's record bookings (separate document) point the same way.

findings.finding: ASMPT, KLIC's main competitor in TCB and wire bonding, reported record Q3 2026 group bookings of HK$8.85B (+138% y/y) on Oct 28, with record C2S/TCB orders on AI demand. It guided Q4 bookings below Q3, citing SMT one-offs and pull-ins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured KLIC reaction to ASMPT prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer, and TCB share between ASMPT and KLIC is uncertain: record ASMPT TCB orders could be share taken from KLIC. The market has not marked KLIC up on it, since the stock fell after Oct 28.

findings.finding: Besi reported Q3 2026 orders of EUR342.6M (+96% y/y) and revenue +114% y/y on Oct 22, with Q4 revenue guided flat +/-5%. Its shares have roughly halved since June on worries about HBM hybrid-bonding adoption timing, the same de-rating KLIC has taken while peer fundamentals stay strong.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector de-rating is about the durability of the cycle, not current orders. A sector-wide multiple compression that has not met an order downturn leaves room for a relief move on a clean guide.
findings.independence: Shares the peer read with the ASMPT finding. Different document.

findings.finding: Amkor, a major OSAT customer for KLIC wire bonders, set full-year 2026 capex at approximately $2.5B in its Oct 26 Q3 release, the bottom of the $2.5-3.0B range it gave in July. Its advanced-products revenue was down y/y ($1,632M vs $1,684M) and Q4 sales are guided to $1.9-2.0B, flat to down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. Customer capex is the direct input to KLIC's equipment orders.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a primary-document capex trim from a direct customer, dated after KLIC last spoke. The 20d drawdown may already hold some of it, but no KLIC preview cites it.
findings.independence: Cuts against the ASE finding: ASE strong, Amkor capex trimmed. This is a different counterparty, so it is not a contradiction of the same fact.

findings.finding: Positioning and sentiment: the stock is $66 against a post-August range of $56.90-103.39 and a 200-day of $86.66, down about 22% since the last report. The Earnings Whispers preview reads sentiment as mildly bullish but price action as cautious. A clean beat and guide lands on a de-rated name, but the semis tape is weak: the SOX fell 10.1% on Nov 5 on post-midterm data-centre fears and a held-up export licence for SK Hynix.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print from depressed levels +19.27%. Aug 2026 print near highs -3.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced by definition: it is the price. The point is asymmetry after a 50% drawdown with 4% short interest. The +24 skew says the market still pays for downside, so the size is kept small.

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call under new CEO Raj Talluri (appointed Aug 17, effective Sept 1, 2026; the stock fell 9.5% on the appointment). A new CEO's first guide and FY27 framing carry reset risk, for example to the FY27 TCB target of $150-200M or with conservative December guidance. Separately, the Oct 13 8-K moved the FY27 incentive plan to Operating Profit and Gross Margin metrics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior call under this CEO. The appointment day was -9.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is known. How he guides is not, and the +24 put skew may already hold part of this risk.
findings.independence: 8-K of 2026-10-14 on the FY27 incentive plan, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56978/000005697826000036/klic-20261013.htm (gross-margin and operating-profit metrics, no numeric targets disclosed)

findings.finding: The whisper EPS of $1.61 sits above the top of the $1.28-1.56 guide and well above the $1.44 consensus, so an in-line or top-of-range quarter may read as a miss on the buy-side bar. Management has raised its guide on every call ($0.33 -> $0.67 -> $1.00 -> $1.42 guided EPS), so the market is conditioned to expect another raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026: beat by $0.14 with a raised guide, and the stock fell 3.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper is public but not the consensus number the wire quotes. A beat on $1.44 will be headlined, while the buy-side bar is higher.
findings.independence: Same document as the positioning finding: two readings of one preview, on different lines.

outside_window.finding: KLIC's expanded Advanced Solutions production facility is due in the second half of FY27, and its hybrid bonding tool ships in the first half of FY27. Both are capacity and product milestones after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: A sourced consensus for the December-quarter (FQ1 FY27) revenue or EPS: none found.
A specific cause of the 5d -9.6% drop: no KLIC-specific news found, only the sector tape.
KLIC 8-Ks since Aug: only the CEO appointment (Aug 17) and the incentive plan (Oct 14). No pre-announcement and no item 2.02.
Form 4 cluster Oct 7-19 (16 filings): not opened; most likely the start-of-year equity grants/vesting tied to the new incentive plan.
KLIC-specific Micron/HBM4 TCB order news in 2026: none found.
Analyst previews for November 2026: none reachable. MarketBeat, Benzinga and Zacks returned 403s.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A report that SK Hynix is slowing its HBM4 ramp to redirect capacity to conventional DRAM, offered as a cause of the chip selloff.
rejected_candidates.detail: The Barchart article was undated in the snippet and the fetch returned empty, so the date cannot be confirmed. The Motley Fool's Nov 5 article attributes the rout to post-midterm fears and the export licence, not HBM.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Analyst price target average of about $62 (Benzinga) against a $115 high (Needham, Aug 6).
rejected_candidates.detail: The aggregator averages disagree ($62 vs $91 vs $107) and mix stale targets, so no usable bar.

baseline_tension: The peer and customer evidence is mostly positive (ASE, ASMPT, Besi orders) and cuts against the 50% drawdown and the +24 put skew. Amkor's capex trim, a new CEO's first guide and an above-guide whisper agree with the skew, so the net lean is roughly flat.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Aug guide raise was sold (-3.39%), so the H1 FY27 demand-commentary finding went from +1.0 to +0.6.

Lesson 5 (a proxy loses to a primary number): ASE's monthly revenue is an OSAT proxy, so it went from +0.8 to +0.6. Amkor's capex is a primary document from a direct customer but a capex narrowing, not a cut, so it went from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lessons 6 and 7 (bar unsourced for the guide line; skew +24 against a mild positive lean): p_up went from 52 to 51. abs_move went from 10.0 to 10.5 on the understatement lesson.
ASMPT, Besi, positioning, CEO and whisper findings left standing.
